archetype.name: Gunslinger (scrambling)
archetype.definition: Maye is a vertical, push-the-ball passer whose value comes from completing throws downfield and extending broken plays with his legs, and he accepts more interceptions than most starters as the cost.

report.headline: A downfield passer having a good year, taking more risk, now sidelined by a fractured fibula.
report.take:
Drake Maye entered 2026 off a top-three season. He ranked 3rd in EPA per play, 3rd in CPOE and 3rd in yards per attempt in 2025. This year he has been good rather than great: 0.132 EPA per dropback (13th of 55), a 6.81 CPOE (5th) and 8.44 yards per attempt (6th). That is still well above a league-average passer, who sits at -0.027 EPA per dropback. The bigger news now is availability. He fractured his right fibula in Week 10 at Detroit after 17% of the snaps, is listed Out with an estimated return of December 27, and sits at QB3 on the depth chart. The Patriots kept him on the 53-man roster rather than IR, which suggests they expect him back this season, not that he is close.

His value is almost all downfield. Throws of 10+ air yards produced 43.9 EPA, more than his 43.1 across every dropback. The 40 deep attempts alone ran at 0.662 EPA each with a 17.5 CPOE and 8 touchdowns. The short game underneath has been efficient (0.265 EPA on 0-9 yard throws). The damage comes from 46 throws behind the line, which cost 23.3 EPA at a 19.6% success rate. Screens and swings that go nowhere are a design-and-blocking problem, and the rushing offense ranks 23rd. His legs add real value: 27 scrambles at 0.622 EPA each, with 17 of them moving the chains.

The gap from last season is turnovers. Interceptions jumped from 0.47 a game to 1.1, and his 4.0% interception rate ranks 46th of 55. The odd part is that his aggressiveness (throws into tight windows) fell from 17.9% to 11.76% and his bad-throw rate improved slightly. So he is not forcing more tight-window throws. The picks cluster on deep and intermediate balls (9 of the 11 at 10+ yards) and to his left (7 picks, -0.059 EPA, against 0.383 going right). Part of that looks like small-sample clumping: the 3-pick games at Seattle and Green Bay. Part looks like a real cost of a longer 3.16-second time to throw behind a line now missing its center and a guard. The money downs lag too. He is below zero on third down (-0.106) and in the red zone (-0.115), well short of what a 2025-caliber Maye produced.

Going forward, his rest of season is a question of whether he plays and how mobile he is. When he returns he should still be an above-average passer whose ceiling comes from deep shots. Expect a less dangerous scrambler on a healing fibula, and probably fewer interceptions than this pace as the clustered picks even out.

strengths.title: Deep-ball accuracy and production
strengths.body: His 20+ yard throws ran at 0.662 EPA with a 17.5 CPOE and 8 touchdowns. That makes the deep ball the engine of the whole passing game. Accuracy over expected on deep balls has been a trait across his 2025 and 2026 numbers, not a hot streak. It will carry over, though 40 attempts means the TD count on those throws is the part most likely to cool.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move the chains
strengths.body: Maye turned 27 scrambles into 0.622 EPA each, with 17 first downs. That rescues dropbacks that would otherwise end in sacks or throwaways. He has ranked inside the top ten in QB rushing yards every year, so the skill is real. A fractured fibula is exactly the injury that could blunt it when he returns.

strengths.title: Accuracy over expected remains top-five
strengths.body: Even down from last year's 10.8, his 6.81 CPOE ranks 5th. On short throws he completes 73.6% at 0.265 EPA. He places the ball better than the throw difficulty predicts, which keeps the offense on schedule when the deep game isn't there.

concerns.title: Interceptions more than doubled
concerns.body: His interception rate of 4.0% ranks 46th, and he is throwing 0.63 more picks a game than in 2025. Nine of the 11 came on throws of 10+ air yards. Because his tight-window rate actually fell, this is partly the price of his downfield style and partly clustering in two three-pick games. It should drift back toward his career norm, but not all the way.

concerns.title: Dead plays behind the line
concerns.body: Throws behind the line of scrimmage cost 23.3 EPA at a 19.6% success rate, and under-center dropbacks ran at -0.21 EPA. That points to scheme and blocking more than Maye: screens getting blown up and a run game ranked 23rd that doesn't sell play-action. It is fixable by design, but it has persisted all year.

concerns.title: Below zero on money downs
concerns.body: He is negative on third down (-0.106 EPA, 36.5% conversions facing 7.2 yards to go) and in the red zone (-0.115). Long third downs reflect the early-down offense. The red-zone dip, 50% completions on 38 attempts, is a small sample and the likeliest to rebound.

trend.note: He opened with three poor games (negative passing EPA against Seattle, Pittsburgh and Jacksonville), then ran five strong ones from Buffalo through Miami. That stretch lifted his last-five EPA per dropback to 0.199. Next came a three-interception loss to Green Bay and the fibula fracture early at Detroit, where his sack rate over the last three games had climbed to 11.4%.

nextGame.headline: Maye is out; the Chargers trip goes on without him
nextGame.body:
Maye will not play at the Chargers. He is listed Out with a fractured fibula and an estimated return of December 27, and he is QB3 on the depth chart. The setup is one he would have liked. Los Angeles ranks 29th against deep passes (0.818 EPA allowed) and 28th in sack rate, which suits a quarterback who lives on 20+ yard throws and has taken 21 sacks. The game is indoors with a 35.5 total, LAC -1.5, and a near-even moneyline. The Book expects a low-scoring game, largely because the Chargers' offense ranks last in EPA.

Availability on both sides matters for the Patriots' passing game, not for Maye himself. New England's receiving corps is thin: A.J. Brown is Doubtful with a hamstring, Romeo Doubs is on IR but may practice this week, and center Ben Brown is Out. Guard Alijah Vera-Tucker was designated to return from IR, which would help whoever starts. On the other side, corner Tarheeb Still (95% of snaps) is Out and linebacker Daiyan Henley (87%) is Out, both openings Maye would have targeted. Justin Herbert is questionable after entering the concussion protocol.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers' leaky deep coverage
keyMatchups.body: Los Angeles allows 0.818 EPA on deep throws, 29th in the league, and is missing its top corner, Still. This is the matchup Maye's game is built for. It will test whether the replacement quarterback can push the ball the way Maye did.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Chargers pass rush
keyMatchups.body: The Chargers rank 28th in sack rate. That would have eased the long-developing dropbacks that produced 8 sacks over Maye's last three games, and it gives a backup a cleaner pocket.

keyMatchups.title: New England's depleted receiver room
keyMatchups.body: With A.J. Brown doubtful and Doubs only possibly practicing, the targets lean on DeMario Douglas and Hunter Henry. Those two were Maye's most efficient options, at 0.484 and 0.541 EPA per target.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Patriots activate a practice window or move Maye to IR. His staying on the 53-man roster is the clearest signal on how soon he returns.

restOfSeason.body: Maye's remaining season depends on a fibula fracture with an estimated return of December 27. That likely leaves only the final weeks, if the bone heals on schedule and the team still has something to play for. When he plays, the passing profile should hold: top-five accuracy over expected and a deep game good enough to carry a below-average run game. Expect interceptions to settle closer to his 2025 rate than his current 4.0%, and the red-zone struggles to improve with more attempts. The expected regression is in his rushing. A quarterback returning from a fractured right fibula is unlikely to scramble as freely early on, so I'd project 12-25 rushing yards a game, below his season level. I'd also expect 205-255 passing yards, roughly 1.3-1.9 touchdowns and 0.6-1.0 interceptions a game, with a weak Patriots defense (24th in EPA) keeping game scripts pass-friendly.
swingFactors: Whether the fibula heals on the December 27 estimate or he is shut down
Mobility on return, which drives the scramble value
Health of A.J. Brown, Doubs and the interior line

confidence.note: Fractured fibula with an uncertain return date and few games likely left in the season.
